rules.rule: Check for urgent injured patient conditions
rules.problem: Trigger is Traumatic injury only, and in this SNOMED release Wound, Fracture of bone and Injury of head are not its descendants (Contusion is). A patient recorded with a wound/fracture/head injury but not 'Traumatic injury' is never asked about confusion, restlessness or weakness, which only this task checks for, so the shock rule's soft criteria can never be collected for them. Consider triggering on (or (Traumatic injury) (Wound) (Fracture of bone) (Injury of head)).

rules.rule: Check for urgent wound conditions in the injured patient
rules.problem: Structure and trigger match the 'Wound and any of' column. 'Pale' from 'cold, pale, numb, no pulse' has no encoding (no suitable SNOMED finding), and Limb ischemia stands in for 'poor perfusion'.

rules.rule: Check for urgent fracture conditions in the injured patient
rules.problem: Matches the 'Fracture and any of' column; 'muscle tightness' is uncoded (no general SNOMED concept) and 'Fracture, open' should be the disorder 'Open fracture'.

rules.rule: Check for urgent head injury conditions in the injured patient
rules.problem: Matches the 'Head injury and any of' column. Mild headache and Clouded consciousness are not urgent conditions but are needed here so the probable concussion rule passes the check_for constraint; the task title is slightly misleading.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable shock in the injured patient
rules.problem: Footnote 1 is a comma list ('If SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely'); the rule reads it as 'any one of'. SBP < 80 alone is supported by the box ('If shock/SBP < 80'), but under this reading restlessness alone or weakness alone after any injury yields a probable Shock diagnosis, which is a strong claim from one soft sign. The page is ambiguous; a clinician should confirm whether the soft signs need a vital-sign criterion as well. Pulse is encoded with 'Pulse, function' rather than a rate observable.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable concussion after head injury
rules.problem: 'If mild headache, dizziness or mental fogginess, concussion likely' under Head injury: type, probable level and or-structure are faithful.

rules.rule: Urgent: injured patient with bruising and blood in urine
rules.problem: Faithful to the 'Bruising and blood in urine' column; Urgent matches 'Give urgent attention'.

rules.rule: Urgent: injured patient with wound danger signs
rules.problem: (and Wound (or ...)) matches 'Wound and any of'; Urgent is justified by the box heading. Limb ischemia imprecision as above.

rules.rule: Urgent: injured patient with fracture danger signs
rules.problem: (and Fracture (or ...)) matches 'Fracture and any of'. Rib enumeration misses a recorded 'Fracture of multiple ribs' with no count; 'Fracture, open' morphology instead of the Open fracture disorder.

rules.rule: Urgent: injured patient with head injury danger signs
rules.problem: Finding of vomiting drops the page's '>= 2 times', so a head injury with a single vomit (a common symptom) is escalated to Urgent; Intoxication (disorder) also pulls in any Poisoning. Everything else in the or-list is faithful to 'Head injury and any of'.

summary: The head-injury priority rule escalates any head injury with a single vomit to Urgent because the page's 'vomiting >= 2 times' lost its count, and the shock rule treats footnote 1's comma list as 'any of', so restlessness or weakness alone after an injury gives a probable Shock diagnosis; both deserve a clinician's eye. Smaller imprecisions: Limb ischemia (a disorder) stands in for the sign 'poor perfusion', 'Fracture, open' is a morphology where the disorder 'Open fracture' exists, Intoxication includes Poisoning, and pulse uses 'Pulse, function' rather than a rate observable. The umbrella task triggers only on Traumatic injury, which in this release does not subsume Wound, Fracture of bone or Injury of head, so its shock-related check_for items are never collected for patients recorded with those more specific findings; the page's same-day referral tier (pregnant, bleeding disorder, anticoagulant, high-speed collision, fall > 3 m) is not encoded at all.
